source: Console & Torasso (1991) A spectrum of logical definitions of model-based diagnosis
finding: Abductive diagnosis (explain all observations) and consistency-based diagnosis (explain none, only stay consistent) are two ends of one spectrum. A parameter OBS+ picks which observations must be explained. Read via Theseider Dupre's restatement, not the original.
numbers: Definition: diagnosis = mode assignment whose predictions are consistent with OBS and imply OBS+. OBS+ empty = consistency-based; OBS+ = OBS is abductive.
limits: Original paper not opened; only the 2000 restatement. No empirical data, a logical result.
agent_relevance: O8 reframe: the agent can choose per observation which must be explained and which only must not contradict the model.

source: Theseider Dupre (2000) Abductive and Consistency-Based Diagnosis Revisited: a Modeling Perspective
finding: For a fully predictive (deterministic) model, abductive and consistency-based diagnosis give identical answers (Property 1). They diverge only when the model is nondeterministic or abstract.
numbers: Property 1 proved in two lines. Qualitative-deviation tank example: a pump fault is consistent with a sign change in level derivative but does not predict it.
limits: Theory paper, no empirical test. Qualitative models only; real-valued domains are rarely fully predictive.
agent_relevance: The abductive vs consistency choice matters mainly when our scaffold's world model is vague. A precise simulator makes the distinction moot.

source: Theseider Dupre (2000) same paper: parametrised assumptions and fixes for weak models
finding: When abduction is too strict because hypotheses do not entail exact observations, three fixes exist: parametrised assumptions (flat(B,V) <-> V in [0,1.2]), Hobbs-style etc-assumptions, or Cordier's weaker 'explain = prediction abstracts observation', which equals consistency.
numbers: Flat battery: voltage 0.8 explained by flat(b1,0.8). Cordier warns of hypothesis proliferation.
limits: Costs: more assumptions to enumerate. Paper does not measure this.
agent_relevance: Tells the agent how to keep abductive checking usable: state hypotheses as ranges, not point predictions.

source: Theseider Dupre (2000) same paper: Kautz supermarket example and closure
finding: Kautz (1987/1991) showed the plan 'get food' does not entail 'going to this supermarket', so pure abduction under-explains. Poole and Reiter closure axioms restore equivalence of abduction and deduction.
numbers: Equivalence under explanatory closure (Poole 1994, Reiter 1991, Konolige 1992).
limits: Closure needs the modeller to write down all causes, a completeness assumption.
agent_relevance: An LLM cannot guarantee a closed cause list, so abductive 'explains everything' claims need an 'other' hypothesis slot.

source: Poole (1993/1994) Representing Diagnosis Knowledge
finding: For acyclic causal domains, the same problem encoded in abductive and in consistency-based form returns the same base causes (Theorem 3.2). Equivalence needs a different knowledge encoding in each framework.
numbers: Theorem 3.2: base causes of abductive diagnoses from KB_A equal those of consistency-based diagnoses from KB_CB. Abductive: c->s is a fact if s is a necessary symptom, else c->s is an assumable hypothesis.
limits: Propositional, acyclic, no time. Poole says the final answer on the representation problem is not given.
agent_relevance: Prompts that ask for 'consistent with' vs 'explains' need different wording of the same knowledge; the same text will not serve both.

source: Poole (1993) same paper: non-strict causation and minimality
finding: Non-strict causes (a cold may cause sneezing) can be represented in both frameworks without new reasoning constructs. Abductive diagnosis is a minimal explanation; consistency-based diagnosis is a minimal set of abnormalities.
numbers: Worked examples with two minimal explanations versus differing consistency diagnoses.
limits: Propositional only. No probabilities.
agent_relevance: Minimality is a tie-break the agent can run in code: prefer fewest abnormal components.

source: Roos (1993/2022) Efficient Model Based Diagnosis
finding: A causal-ancestor focus method picks likely broken components and the most informative probe, worst case O(n^2) in components, near linear for low connectivity.
numbers: Worst case O(n^2); linear if connectivity is low.
limits: Abstract and intro read in detail; no benchmark data. Not LLM.
agent_relevance: Diagnosis search can be pruned by causal ancestry before asking a model anything.

source: Wikipedia (accessed 2026) Abductive reasoning
finding: Logic-based abduction: T plus E entails O and is consistent; minimality added; best explanation picked by simplicity, prior or explanatory power. Set-cover abduction reduces to covering when effects are independent. Base rate and prosecutor's fallacy named as sources of diagnostic error.
numbers: No performance figures given for Internist-I. Infer (bi-abduction) reportedly prevented thousands of bugs.
limits: Encyclopedia; first 100000 of 159634 chars read. Does not use the 'Ab' predicate wording.
agent_relevance: Background only. Base-rate neglect is a known risk when ranking abductive hypotheses without priors.

source: Salimi et al. (2026) Wiring the Why: survey of abductive reasoning in LLMs
finding: Defines abduction as two stages: generate hypotheses, then select. Own benchmark of 3B-72B open and proprietary models shows closed-form selection is nearly solved but generation and long narratives are not.
numbers: ART and e-CARE selection best 87.2-88.0%. DDXPlus ranking 79.75% Top-1, 98.7% Hit@3; same diagnosis as open generation 63.0 Hit@3, 28.1 Set-F1@3. True Detective best 42.9%, MuSR murder 68.0%, ProofWriter best 21.5% accuracy.
limits: Single direct prompt template; no controlled same-model cross-type test; authors urge caution on the abduction vs deduction comparison.
agent_relevance: Stage I/II gap is the key: picking among candidates is easy, producing the right candidate is hard. Supply candidate lists by code or retrieval.

source: Salimi et al. (2026) same survey: abduction vs deduction across the literature
finding: Pooled accuracy across published (model, method, dataset) points: deduction median 79.96%, abduction 42.50%, induction 28.8%. Strong deduction does not imply strong abduction.
numbers: Abduction spread reaches near zero. Most paired points: abduction under 50% with deduction over 60%.
limits: Vote-count pooling, mixed prompts and datasets, few paired points. Not a formal meta-analysis.
agent_relevance: Do not assume a model that checks logic well will diagnose well.

source: Holzer et al. (2026) TempoBench: Reasoning Execution Without Causal Attribution Is Just Simulation
finding: Formally verified benchmark from Mealy machines. Models simulate forward well but fail to say which inputs were necessary for an output (SIM/MIN gap). This is the core step of simulate a model and compare with observation.
numbers: DeepSeek R1: 96.0% step accuracy on forward simulation, 32.1% on minimal necessary causes. Over 94.9% of wrong MIN steps are overspecification: Sonnet 4.6 94.9%, V3 96.5%, Haiku 4.5 99.8%.
limits: Synthetic automata (SYNTCOMP specs); one fixed seed for fine-tuning, no variance or significance tests; strict exact-set scoring.
agent_relevance: Our simulator should be code. Ask the model only for hypotheses, never for which cause was necessary.

source: Holzer et al. (2026) TempoBench: visibility ablation
finding: Hiding part of the transition table wrecks simulation but barely moves causal attribution, which suggests attribution is answered by copying visible guards rather than by reasoning.
numbers: SIM falls 79.5% to 31.8% (V3.2 no reasoning), 66.9% to 28.8% (reasoning), 59.8% to 8.8% (fine-tuned LLaMA-8B) at 25% visibility. MIN+ moves at most 3.4 points. Guard copied on 96.5% of MIN steps.
limits: Mechanistic reading is the authors' interpretation of output patterns.
agent_relevance: A model may answer why by pattern retrieval. Require a code-run counterfactual (O8 check) before accepting a causal story.

source: Holzer et al. (2026) TempoBench: fine-tuning transfer
finding: Fine-tuning on TempoBench lifts external causal benchmarks while matching general reasoning on standard ones.
numbers: CLadder NIE +19.6 points (LLaMA-3.1-8B) and +7.5 (Qwen2.5-7B) versus matched non-TempoBench recipe; CauGym CDE +0.0 and -4.0. About 110 GPU-hours training.
limits: Single seed, no significance tests, small open models.
agent_relevance: Training is out of scope for our scaffold; shows the gap is learnable but not prompt-fixable.

source: Fang et al. (2026) OpenRCA 2.0: From Outcome Labels to Causal Process Supervision
finding: Scoring the causal path instead of only the root-cause label reveals ungrounded diagnoses: right service named, no valid propagation path. 11 frontier LLMs.
numbers: Exact-match root-cause set 20.7%; F1 34.1%; names a correct service 76.0%; Recall 33.2%; valid path (PR) 61.5%; Node F1 62.2% vs Edge F1 43.4%. Sonnet 4.6 PR/AnySvc 66% vs Qwen3.6-Max 91%.
limits: Fault-injection datasets, 3 microservice systems, 44 services; the PAVE annotation protocol is itself new.
agent_relevance: Grade the explanation chain, not just the label. Key for G3: a right answer with a wrong path should not pass.

source: Fang et al. (2026) OpenRCA 2.0: three failure patterns
finding: Agents commit early, weight visible activity, and chase the loudest signal. Silence from a killed pod is read as health.
numbers: Patterns: premature commitment (stop after one cause, miss the subtle second fault), presence bias, salience capture (about 24 points of AnySvc shortfall).
limits: Qualitative reading of a stratified sample of 11-model trajectories.
agent_relevance: These are classic abductive traps (single hypothesis, absence read as normal). Add a forced check of what absence of signal would mean.

source: Kim et al. (2026) Why Do AI Agents Systematically Fail at Cloud RCA?
finding: 1,675 runs (335 OpenRCA tasks x 5 models) classified into 12 pitfalls. Failures are shared across models and come from the framework, not the model.
numbers: Hallucination in interpretation 71.2%, incomplete exploration 63.9%, symptom-as-cause 39.9%, no cross-validation 18.6%. Baseline perfect-detection accuracy 3.9-12.5% overall. 11.1 steps per run, about 1.38B tokens, about $1,394.
limits: Classification by a Claude Opus 4.5 agent with human verification; mitigation tested on Bank subset only (70 tasks for prompts).
agent_relevance: Symptom-as-cause is the same error as stopping at the first abductive explanation.

source: Kim et al. (2026) same paper: mitigation experiments
finding: Prompt fixes did not help; structure did. Hypothesis-driven prompting widened exploration but interpretation errors stayed. Pitfall-aware prompts were acknowledged in the trace and ignored in practice. Passing code and raw errors between agents helped.
numbers: Prompt tests: Claude Sonnet 4, 70 Bank tasks, no meaningful gain. Enriched protocol: pitfalls down about 14-15 points (GPT-5 mini, Sonnet 4); perfect detections GPT-5 mini 0 to 2 (0.0% to 4.9%), Gemini 2.5 Pro 1 to 3 (2.4% to 7.3%); steps -22.1%, time -22.3%, tokens -1.6%.
limits: Very small counts (0-3 cases). Four models. Bank only.
agent_relevance: Supports G2 and the design where the program decides and the model fills slots: show raw outputs, do not trust self-described pitfalls.

source: Wang et al. (2026) Cloud-OpsBench
finding: Ten LLM agents, 754 cases, 57 fault types. Outcome-correct diagnoses often lack closed evidence chains. Reusing past trajectories or SOPs helps on one system, less on the other.
numbers: Best Joint RCA Accuracy 0.76 (OnlineBoutique), 0.68 (TrainTicket); Evidence Closure Rate 0.38 and 0.15. Trajectory-as-ICL, DeepSeek-V4-Flash: JRA 0.76 to 0.83, ECR 0.38 to 0.57. Gains on TrainTicket smaller and mixed.
limits: Two benchmark systems; failure categories from a purposive sample.
agent_relevance: Independent confirmation of OpenRCA 2.0: label accuracy overstates grounded diagnosis.

source: Gong et al. (2026) ORCA-bench: How Ready Are LM Agents for Oncall?
finding: 1,079 RCA tasks with six days of OpenTelemetry data; five frontier coding agents. Low accuracy and frequent invented causes.
numbers: Best RCA accuracy 25.3% Medium, 10.0% Hard, 58.7% Easy (Sonnet 4.6). Hallucinated root cause in 7% (DeepSeek-V4-Pro) to 40% (GLM-5) of reports. Removing source code cuts accuracy 9-16 points. 26-40% of telemetry calls fail or return empty. Judge agreement w 0.91 vs humans.
limits: LLM judge (GPT-5.4); benchmark from an industry vendor; synthetic feature-flag faults.
agent_relevance: Add an unknown output and penalise invented causes; tool failures can look like evidence of absence.

source: Qi et al. (2026) R2Act: Can LLMs Really Recover Microservice Failures?
finding: Right diagnosis does not give right action. 302 Kubernetes incidents.
numbers: Best RAG LLMs: root-cause service 91.4-99.7%, recovery validity 36.8-60.3%. Invalid plans for 39.5-62.0% of correctly diagnosed incidents. LogPrompt: RCA-Service above 55%, validity near 12%. NB: 6.6% to 46.0% validity with full evidence.
limits: Benchmark built by the authors; action space is incident-specific and constructed.
agent_relevance: Diagnosis is one step. After an explanation, the agent must test the repair against the model.

source: Constantinov et al. (2026) LATS-RCA
finding: Tree search over root-cause hypotheses beats linear ReAct on a small benchmark. Gain comes from breadth of hypotheses, not more evidence.
numbers: Light-OAuth2: 91.3% (SD 1.2 over 5 runs) vs single ReAct 39.8%, multi-agent ReAct 57.4%. Hypotheses explored 18.9 vs 5.1 and 8.5; evidence items about 7.0 for all. Cost 53.1 calls, 156K tokens, 9.1 min vs 13.5 calls, 41K, 1.2 min. Real production: 24.1 of 37 incidents (65.1%, range 62-70%).
limits: Baselines built by the authors; synthetic LO2 faults; production run only 37 incidents with no baseline; about 4x cost.
agent_relevance: Wider hypothesis sets help, bought with compute. Gate extra branches by G1 signals, not by default.

source: He et al. (2025) GEAR: General Evaluation for Abductive Reasoning
finding: Reference-free scoring of a hypothesis SET on consistency, generalizability, diversity. Single gold answers hide that many explanations fit the data (underdetermination).
numbers: Nine LLMs, four benchmarks (MINI-ARC, ACRE, List Functions, ARC-2025): 70B-class models give only about 20% consistent hypotheses; consistent ones cover about 95% of the sample space; model size weakly related to diversity; consistency not correlated with number of initial I/O pairs.
limits: Program-synthesis style tasks; consistent hypotheses concentrated in o1 and o4-mini.
agent_relevance: Check consistency in code before accepting any hypothesis; do not trust the model's own claim.

source: Yang et al. (2026) Auditing evaluation artifacts and data leakage in LLM rare disease diagnosis
finding: Replicated the agentic system DeepRare. Scores held under the original one-vs-rest protocol and fell under strict isolation. Leakage inflation exceeded the agent's real gain.
numbers: Mean Recall@1 54.3% (SD 18.2) to 40.3% (SD 11.1), Hedges g 0.94. MME 75% to 42%, PUMCH 66% to 42%, ZJUMCH 39% to 30% (p<0.05 McNemar). Agent gain over zero-shot LLM g 0.77/0.81/1.01 (R@1/3/5); leakage inflation g 0.94/1.18/1.21. Supervised classifiers 42.9% to 16.7% (d 2.01). Over 60,000 cases.
limits: Single agentic system reconstructed; two other backbones show the same pattern in the supplement.
agent_relevance: Our own tests (G3) need held-out cases; retrieval over a pool that holds the answer's neighbours fakes diagnostic skill.

source: Search listing: arXiv 2609.20620 AUV fault recovery simulation platform
finding: Listing says a frontier model places the true cause in its top three 85-90% of the time versus 60-78% for local models over 480 trials.
numbers: 85-90% vs 60-78% top-3 (listing only, not verified).
limits: Not opened; verify before use.
agent_relevance: Possible example of simulate-then-diagnose in robotics.

source: Search listing: arXiv 2605.08011 PACS, abductive reasoning with probabilistic commonsense
finding: Listing says an LLM-plus-solver proof sampler beats chain-of-thought on abduction tasks.
numbers: No numbers read.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Candidate for neuro-symbolic abduction; read before citing.

source: Search listing: arXiv 2509.10401 Abduct, Act, Predict (A2P)
finding: Listing says causal failure attribution in multi-agent systems reaches 47.46% step accuracy vs 16.67% baseline.
numbers: 47.46% vs 16.67% (listing only).
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Closest published LLM use of an abduct-act-predict loop; verify.
